judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: #realname is the visible 'Name *' field of a support form that asks for the user's own name. Its markup (<input type="text" id="realname" name="realname" required>) has no autocomplete attribute, so its purpose is not programmatically identified. autocomplete="name" is the matching input purpose from the WCAG list. This fails 1.3.5.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: #website is a spam honeypot, not a field that collects information about the user. Its label and the input sit at x/y -9999 (snapshot state 'offscreen'), it has tabindex=-1 and autocomplete=off, and it does not appear in the screenshot. 1.3.5 only covers inputs that collect information about the user, and people are meant to leave this one empty. The suggested autocomplete="url" would make browsers fill the trap and get real users flagged as spam.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: #email asks for the user's own email address: the helper text says 'otherwise, we will not be able to respond to you'. It has type="email" but no autocomplete attribute. Under 1.3.5, type=email only sets the input format. It does not say the address belongs to the user, which is what autocomplete="email" does. Leaving autocomplete out fails 1.3.5.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: #website is a hidden honeypot (offscreen at -9999, tabindex=-1, autocomplete=off, not shown in the screenshot). 3.3.2 applies when content requires user input, and this field is meant to stay empty. It already has a programmatic label, <label for="website">Website *</label>, hidden offscreen together with the input, so the suggested patch adds a duplicate of a label that already exists. Exposing a honeypot to screen readers can be an accessibility problem, but it is not a missing label or instructions under 3.3.2.
